instructions: Open book. Answer each item from the saved AWS pages and the fact canon only. Give citations for every label: why the key is right and why each other option is wrong. A citation is a fact id or {source_id, quote} with a verbatim quote. Set flag when a second answer is defensible, else null.

items.stem: A company uses AWS Organizations with all features enabled and has 25 member accounts in several organizational units (OUs). The administrators of each member account have the AdministratorAccess policy and can edit the IAM policies of their account. Last month, one member account left the organization without approval, and the company lost its billing and security controls over that account. The company must ensure that no member account can leave the organization again. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Replace the AdministratorAccess policy in every member account with a customer managed policy that leaves out the organizations:LeaveOrganization action.

options.label: B
options.text: Create an SCP that denies the organizations:LeaveOrganization action, and attach the SCP directly to every member account as each account joins.

options.label: C
options.text: Create an SCP that denies the organizations:LeaveOrganization action, and attach the SCP to the management account of the organization.

options.label: D
options.text: Create an SCP that denies the organizations:LeaveOrganization action, and attach the SCP to the root of the organization.

items.stem: A company uses AWS Organizations with all features enabled. To protect its logs, the security team attaches an SCP to the root of the organization. The SCP denies the logs:DeleteLogGroup action. A week later, an engineer signs in to the management account, uses an IAM role that has the AdministratorAccess policy, and deletes an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group in that account. The call succeeds. What is the reason that the call succeeds?

options.label: A
options.text: SCPs do not restrict the users or roles in the management account of the organization.

options.label: B
options.text: SCPs restrict the IAM users in an account but not the IAM roles in that account.

options.label: C
options.text: The AdministratorAccess policy of the role overrides the Deny statement of the SCP.

options.label: D
options.text: An SCP on the root applies to an account only after it is also attached to that account.

items.stem: A company uses AWS Organizations with all features enabled. The root of the organization has the FullAWSAccess SCP. In the Workloads organizational unit (OU), the company replaced FullAWSAccess with an allow-list SCP that allows only Amazon EC2, Amazon S3, and Amazon CloudWatch actions. One account in the Workloads OU now needs Amazon Athena. The account has FullAWSAccess attached directly, and the IAM role of its analytics team allows Athena actions. Every other account in the Workloads OU must keep the current allow list. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Keep the account in the Workloads OU, and attach an SCP that allows Athena actions directly to the account, next to FullAWSAccess.

options.label: B
options.text: Create a new OU under the root with an SCP that allows Amazon EC2, Amazon S3, CloudWatch, and Athena, and move the account there.

options.label: C
options.text: Create a new account in a new OU whose SCPs allow Athena, and migrate the workloads and data of the account to the new account.

options.label: D
options.text: Keep the account in the Workloads OU, and add Athena actions to the allow-list SCP that is attached to the Workloads OU.

items.stem: A company runs its development, test, and production workloads in one AWS account. An audit finds that developers can change production resources. The company must isolate production from the other environments, keep its audit logs in a separate account, and apply the same security guardrails to every account that it creates in the future. The company does not have a multi-account environment yet. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Create an AWS Control Tower landing zone, and use Account Factory to create separate accounts for the production and non-production workloads.

options.label: B
options.text: Keep one account, and create a separate VPC for each environment, with no network path between the production VPC and the other VPCs.

options.label: C
options.text: Create an organization in AWS Organizations, create each account by hand, and deploy a security baseline to every account with AWS CloudFormation StackSets.

options.label: D
options.text: Keep one account, tag every resource with its environment, and use IAM policies with tag conditions and permissions boundaries to separate the teams.

items.stem: A company has 12 AWS accounts. Each account receives its own bill, and each team owns one or more of the accounts. The finance team wants one bill for all accounts, volume pricing that is based on the combined usage of all accounts, and a monthly cost report for each team. Every team already tags its resources with a team tag. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

options.label: A
options.text: Activate the team tag as a user-defined cost allocation tag in the Billing console of the management account.

options.label: B
options.text: Create an organization, create 12 new member accounts in it, and migrate the workloads of each team into the new accounts.

options.label: C
options.text: Create an organization in AWS Organizations from one account, and invite the other accounts to join the organization.

options.label: D
options.text: Activate the team tag as a user-defined cost allocation tag in the Billing console of each member account.

options.label: E
options.text: Attach an SCP to the root of the organization that allows the billing and cost management actions for every team.

items.stem: A company uses AWS Organizations. Administrators in the management account manage member accounts by assuming the OrganizationAccountAccessRole IAM role in each account. Last month, the company invited an existing AWS account that another business unit used before, and the account accepted the invitation. When an administrator tries to assume OrganizationAccountAccessRole in the invited account, the request fails. What is the reason for the failure?

options.label: A
options.text: An SCP on the root of the organization blocks the management account from assuming roles in member accounts.

options.label: B
options.text: The role is created in an invited account only after the account approves the request to enable all features.

options.label: C
options.text: Organizations creates this role only in accounts that it creates, not in accounts that join by invitation.

options.label: D
options.text: The role is created in an invited account only after an administrator moves the account into an OU.

items.stem: A company uses AWS Organizations with all features enabled. The company stores confidential data in Amazon S3 buckets in many member accounts, and teams create new buckets every week. A security review adds a new rule: principals in the company's accounts must not access S3 buckets that belong to other AWS organizations. The rule must apply to every current and future member account. Which solution will restrict this access with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Set a permissions boundary on every IAM role in every member account that denies Amazon S3 actions on buckets that belong to other organizations.

options.label: B
options.text: Attach a resource control policy (RCP) to the root that denies Amazon S3 actions unless the principal belongs to the company's organization, based on the aws:PrincipalOrgID condition key.

options.label: C
options.text: Add a statement to the bucket policy of every S3 bucket in every member account that denies access to principals outside the company's organization.

options.label: D
options.text: Attach a service control policy (SCP) to the root that denies Amazon S3 actions unless the bucket belongs to the company's organization, based on the aws:ResourceOrgID condition key.

items.stem: A company uses AWS Control Tower to govern its accounts in AWS Organizations. The security team finds that some teams create accounts with the AWS Organizations CreateAccount API in an organizational unit (OU) that is not registered with Control Tower. The controls of the landing zone do not apply to these accounts. The company must make sure that every future account gets the landing zone controls automatically. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Deploy AWS Config rules that match the landing zone controls to the OU with AWS CloudFormation StackSets and automatic deployment to new accounts.

options.label: B
options.text: Use an Amazon EventBridge rule and an AWS Lambda function that copy the control SCPs and AWS Config rules to each account that CreateAccount creates.

options.label: C
options.text: Turn on more detective controls in the landing zone, so that the controls also apply to the accounts in the OU that is not registered.

options.label: D
options.text: Register the OU with AWS Control Tower, enroll the existing accounts of the OU, and create every new account with Account Factory.

items.stem: A company uses AWS Control Tower. The accounts in the Workloads organizational unit (OU) hold Amazon S3 buckets that store audit logs. Developers in these accounts deploy changes with the AWS Management Console and the AWS CLI. The company must prevent every principal in the Workloads OU accounts from deleting the audit log buckets. An alert after a deletion is not enough. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Turn on a preventive control for the Workloads OU in AWS Control Tower, so that an SCP denies the deletion of the audit log buckets.

options.label: B
options.text: Turn on a detective control for the Workloads OU in AWS Control Tower, so that an AWS Config rule reports the deletion of the audit log buckets.

options.label: C
options.text: Create an SCP that denies the deletion of the audit log buckets, and attach the SCP in AWS Organizations to each account of the Workloads OU.

options.label: D
options.text: Turn on a proactive control for the Workloads OU in AWS Control Tower, so that a CloudFormation hook checks the deletion of the audit log buckets.

items.stem: A company uses AWS Organizations. A network team uses a network account to centrally manage one VPC, including the route tables and the NAT gateways. Application teams in six other accounts of the organization must launch Amazon EC2 instances into subnets of this VPC. Each team must own its instances in its own account. The network team must keep full control of the route tables and the NAT gateways. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Share the subnets of the VPC with the IAM roles of the application teams through AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM).

options.label: B
options.text: Share the subnets of the VPC with the six application accounts through AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM).

options.label: C
options.text: Create a VPC in each application account, connect each VPC to the central VPC with VPC peering, and manage the routes through a cross-account role.

options.label: D
options.text: Create an IAM role in the network account that the application teams assume to launch their instances into the subnets of the VPC.

items.stem: A company uses AWS Organizations with all features enabled. The company stores confidential data in Amazon S3 buckets in many member accounts, and teams create new buckets every week. A security review adds a new rule: principals outside the company's organization must not access the company's S3 buckets, even when a bucket policy allows them. The rule must apply to every current and future member account. Which solution will restrict this access with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Attach a service control policy (SCP) to the root that denies Amazon S3 actions unless the bucket belongs to the company's organization, based on the aws:ResourceOrgID condition key.

options.label: B
options.text: Add a statement to the bucket policy of every S3 bucket in every member account that denies access to principals outside the company's organization.

options.label: C
options.text: Set a permissions boundary on every IAM role in every member account that denies Amazon S3 actions on buckets that belong to other organizations.

options.label: D
options.text: Attach a resource control policy (RCP) to the root that denies Amazon S3 actions unless the principal belongs to the company's organization, based on the aws:PrincipalOrgID condition key.

items.stem: A company uses AWS Organizations with all features enabled and adds new member accounts every month. A network team uses a network account to centrally manage Amazon Route 53 Resolver rules that every account must use, including future accounts. An administrator turned on trusted access for AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) in the AWS Organizations console. When the administrator tries to share the rules with the whole organization, the share fails. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

options.label: A
options.text: Share the Resolver rules with the account ID of each member account, and ask each account to accept the invitation that AWS RAM sends.

options.label: B
options.text: Attach an SCP to the root of the organization that allows all AWS RAM actions, and then share the Resolver rules with the organization again.

options.label: C
options.text: Add a resource-based policy to the Resolver rules that lists the account ID of every member account, and update the policy for each new account.

options.label: D
options.text: Enable sharing with AWS Organizations in the AWS RAM console, and then share the Resolver rules with the organization in one resource share.
